description: Check whether the PrizePicks API is available and ready to accept requests.
One league's whole board of player projections, filtered, sorted and paged, with every line fully joined.

parameters.name: league
parameters.description:
**Which league's board to read.** Required on every board endpoint.

Accepts either the league **name** or its numeric **id**, and the name is case-insensitive  -  `NBA`,
`nba` and `7` all reach the same board.

**Board sizes move with the sports calendar**  -  an out-of-season league is a real league with zero
lines on it, not an error. Call `/leagues?with_projections_only=true` for the leagues that actually
have something on the board right now, and sort by `projections_count` to find the busiest.

**Very large boards may not support a board-wide read.** If one returns `503`, narrow the request
with `player_id` or `external_game_id`, or use `/projections-by-ids` or `/projection-details`.
The affected leagues move with the sports calendar, so discover them from `/leagues` rather than
hard-coding a list.

The catalogue includes period splits (`NFL1H`, `WNBA1Q`, `EPL2H`) and season-long markets
(`NFLSZN`, `NBASZN`). A name that does not match returns a `404` naming the
endpoint that lists them, never an empty success payload.

parameters.name: player_name
parameters.description:
**Filter to one athlete by name.** Optional. Case-insensitive substring, matched against both
the player's full name and their display name.

Examples: `Tatum`, `jayson tatum`, `Judge`. A partial surname is usually enough and is safer
than a full name  -  rosters spell accents and suffixes inconsistently.

For an exact, unambiguous lookup use `player_id` instead, or call `/player-projections`, which
returns the athlete's whole slate in one call.

parameters.name: player_id
parameters.description:
**Filter to one athlete by id.** Optional. Digits only, e.g. `59107`.

This is the platform's own player id, and it is the exact-match counterpart to `player_name`.
Read one off any projection's `player.id`, or off `/players`.

Player ids are global  -  the same athlete keeps the same id across every league they appear in
 -  but a board is still read one league at a time, so `league` stays required.

**Prefer this over `player_name` on very large boards.** An exact id allows the API to perform a
narrow lookup without requiring a board-wide read, so it can remain available when a name search
or an unfiltered request is not.

parameters.name: team
parameters.description:
**Filter to one team.** Optional. Case-insensitive substring, matched against the team
abbreviation, the nickname and the market.

So `BOS`, `Celtics` and `Boston` all reach the same rows. Abbreviations are the platform's own
(`BOS`, `NE`, `PIT`)  -  call `/teams?league=NBA` for the exact set on a board.

Because it is a substring match, a short string can over-match across sports (`LA` catches both
Los Angeles clubs). Prefer the nickname when you want exactly one club.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description:
**Filter to one roster position.** Optional. Exact match, case-insensitive.

Positions are **per-sport vocabularies**, spelled the way the platform spells them: `QB`, `RB`,
`WR`, `TE` in football; `F-G`, `G`, `C`, `F-C` in basketball; `SP`, `RP`, `C`, `1B` in baseball.
Combination slots use a hyphen (`F-G`), not a slash.

Read the live vocabulary for a board off `/players?league=NBA` rather than assuming a spelling  - 
an unmatched position returns an empty page, not an error.

parameters.name: stat_type
parameters.description:
**Filter to one stat market, exactly.** Optional. Case-insensitive exact match against both the
stat name and its display name.

Stat markets are **per-league vocabularies**, not one global list. Examples include `Points`,
`Assists`, `Rebounds`, `Pts+Asts`, `Rush Yards`, and `Strikeouts`; the available set changes by
league and as boards change.

Call `/stat-types?league=NBA` for the exact list before filtering. For a prefix or family match
(`Pts+` to catch all three combination markets) use `stat_type_contains` instead.

Combine it with `stat_type` only if you mean both conditions  -  they narrow, they do not widen.

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description:
**Filter to one scoring period.** Optional. Exact match, case-insensitive, against the period
a line is scored over  -  `Full`, `1st Half`, `1Q`, `MAPS 1-2`, `1+2 Innings`, `MAP 4`.

Most boards use one period and this changes nothing on them; it matters when the same athlete and
stat are posted over different windows, such as multiple maps, halves, quarters, or inning ranges.

**Read the exact vocabulary for a board off `/board-summary`'s `counts_by_duration`** rather than
guessing a spelling  -  the values are per-sport and are spelled the way the platform spells them
(`1st Half` on the football half board, `1H` on the football-league half board). An unmatched
value returns an empty page, not an error.

parameters.name: odds_type
parameters.description:
**Filter by the Demon/Goblin dimension.** Optional. This is the field a plain line feed leaves
out, and it is what makes a line comparable to a price.

- `demon`  -  a harder line at a bigger payout
- `goblin`  -  an easier line at a smaller payout
- `standard`  -  the normal line

A PrizePicks entry carries a line rather than a price, so `odds_type` plus `line_score` is how
you reason about value here  -  an odds aggregator that only republishes the number cannot tell
you which of the three you are looking at.

parameters.name: projection_type
parameters.description:
**Filter by what kind of projection it is.** Optional. Two values, spelled as the platform
spells them (spaced and title-cased, not snake_case):

- `Single Stat`  -  one measurable stat for one athlete
- `Fantasy Score`  -  a composite fantasy total rather than a raw stat

Filter to `Fantasy Score` when you want the composite markets isolated; most callers want the
default, which is both.

parameters.name: event_type
parameters.description:
**Filter by what the line is attached to.** Optional. Six values:

- `team`  -  an athlete in a specific fixture, the ordinary case
- `seasonal`  -  a season-long total, the `…SZN` league boards
- `matchup`  -  one athlete measured against another
- `team_with_duration`  -  scoped to a period or inning (see `duration` on each row)
- `combo`  -  a combined line across more than one athlete
- `event`  -  attached to an event rather than a fixture (a race, a card)

Use `seasonal` to separate futures from same-day action  -  they otherwise sit on the same board
with start times months apart.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
**Filter by the line's own lifecycle state.** Optional. Case-insensitive exact match against
the projection's `status` field, e.g. `pre_game`.

This is deliberately **not** a closed list. The platform can add or expose states as its boards
change, so rejecting an unlisted value could block a state the source accepts. An unmatched value
returns an empty page instead.

**It is not the live signal, and this trips people up.** Rows on events already under way keep
`status: "pre_game"` on this host. Use `live_only` or `in_game` for in-play lines. It is also a
different field from `game.status`, which is the FIXTURE's state and spells itself with a
hyphen (`pre-game`, `scheduled`) rather than an underscore.

parameters.name: promo_only
parameters.description:
**Keep only promotional and discounted lines.** Optional; unset returns everything.

Set `true` to isolate rows the platform is running a promotion on. Those rows carry
`flash_sale_line_score` (the discounted number), `discount_name` (e.g. `free_square`) and
`discount_percentage` alongside the ordinary `line_score`, so you can see both what the line was
and what it became.

Promotions are rare and short-lived, so an empty result here usually means "no promo running right
now", not a broken filter.
`/promo-projections` is the same filter as a dedicated endpoint.

than spread across the main ones, so pair this with the right `league`. `/live-projections` is the
same filter as a dedicated endpoint.

Lines with **no** `line_score` are excluded whenever either bound is set. A `0` line score is a
real, playable line and is never treated as missing.

parameters.name: starts_after
parameters.description:
**Only events starting at or after this instant.** Optional. ISO 8601, e.g.
`2026-09-09T00:00:00Z` or `2026-09-09T20:20:00-04:00`.

Compared as an instant, not as text, so an offset-bearing timestamp and a `Z` timestamp for the
same moment behave identically. The platform sends its own start times with a zone offset
(`2026-10-20T15:10:00.000-04:00`).

Pair with `starts_before` for a slate window. A season-long league such as `NFLSZN` has start
times months out, so a narrow window on those boards legitimately returns nothing.

are played in.

An unparseable timestamp is rejected rather than ignored, so a malformed window can never
silently return the whole board.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
**How to order the results.** Optional; defaults to `rank` on the general boards and to
`trending_count` on `/trending-projections`. Leave it unset to get each endpoint's own default
ordering  -  naming a key here overrides it.

- `rank`  -  the platform's own board ordering, so an unsorted page looks like the app's board
- `line_score`  -  the number the line is set at (points, yards, goals  -  whatever the stat is)
- `start_time`  -  when the event tips off; pair with `desc` for the furthest-out lines
- `trending_count`  -  how many players have picked it; the popularity signal
- `player_name`  -  alphabetical by athlete
- `stat_type`  -  groups every "Rebounds" line together, then every "Points" line
- `updated_at`  -  most recently re-priced last, or first with `desc`; the freshness ordering

Sorting is stable, and rows missing the sort key are placed last in **both** directions, so a
line with no `trending_count` never displaces one that has a real value.

description: Re-read up to 200 known projections in one call  -  the watchlist endpoint.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description:
**Up to 200 projection ids in one call, comma-separated.** Required.

Example: `13976084,13975930,13975899`. Whitespace around the commas is fine; duplicates are
collapsed.

This is a genuine bulk lookup  -  one request to the platform, one billable call, up to 200 lines
back, fully joined with their player, team, league, game and stat-type records. It is the right way
to re-read a watchlist of lines you already hold ids for, and it is **not** league-scoped: ids from
different leagues can be mixed freely in one call.

partially-settled watchlist still returns everything that is still live. Compare the returned ids
against what you sent to see which lines have come off the board.

More than 200 ids is rejected rather than truncated, so a caller never believes they received a
full set when they received a capped one.

`trending_count` on `/trending-projections`. Leave it unset to get each endpoint's own default

- `line_score`  -  the number the line is set at (points, yards, goals  -  whatever the stat is)
- `start_time`  -  when the event tips off; pair with `desc` for the furthest-out lines

line with no `trending_count` never displaces one that has a real value.

- `under_or_over`  -  playable in both directions
- `over`  -  over-only

is not a third bucket, and folding it into one of the two would publish a wager direction the
platform never stated.

the projection's `status` field, e.g. `pre_game`.

change, so rejecting an unlisted value could block a state the source accepts. An unmatched value
returns an empty page instead.

hyphen (`pre-game`, `scheduled`) rather than an underscore.

game_id.description:
**Filter to one fixture by its internal id.** Optional. Digits only, e.g. `181166`.

This is the platform's own numeric game id  -  the `game.id` on every projection and the `id` on
every row of `/games`. It is the shorter of the two game identifiers the platform carries.

address the same fixture; use whichever you already have.

external_game_id.description:
**Filter to one fixture by its feed key.** Optional. The long form, e.g.
`NBA_game_MXorbpoalrXOT11KmdzI3Vn6`.

`external_game_id` on `/games` and on every projection's `game` object. It is stable across the
life of a fixture and is the id to key on if you are joining against your own schedule data.

large boards.** The feed key allows a narrow lookup without requiring a board-wide read, so it

**Keep only promotional and discounted lines.** Optional; unset returns everything.

and what it became.

Promotions are rare and short-lived, so an empty result here usually means "no promo running right
now", not a broken filter.
`/promo-projections` is the same filter as a dedicated endpoint.

live_only.description:
**Keep only lines on events already in play.** Optional; unset returns everything.

Set `true` to isolate in-play lines. **Do not filter on `status` for this**  -  the platform leaves

than spread across the main ones, so pair this with the right `league`. `/live-projections` is the
same filter as a dedicated endpoint.

in_game.description:
**Split pre-game lines from in-play lines.** Optional, and it is a three-state filter.

- unset  -  return both
- `true`  -  only lines on events already under way
- `false`  -  only lines on events that have not started

`true` for the in-play slice  -  which is what `live_only` does, from the other side.

**Keep only lines the platform flags as today's action.** Optional; unset returns everything.

Set `true` to trim a board down to the current slate. This reads the platform's own `today` flag
rather than comparing timestamps, so it follows the platform's notion of a sports day  -  which does
not end at midnight and is not your time zone's.

For an explicit window instead, use `starts_after` and `starts_before`.

**Only lines set at or above this number.** Optional, inclusive.

The unit is whatever the stat is  -  points, yards, goals, strikeouts  -  so a bound is only
meaningful alongside a `stat_type`. `stat_type=Points&min_line_score=25` is a question; a bare

real, playable line and is never treated as missing.

**Only lines set at or below this number.** Optional, inclusive.

bound a single `stat_type` or the number means nothing.

Lines with no `line_score` are excluded whenever either bound is set.

that line. It is PrizePicks-native crowd data, not a sportsbook handle split, and no competitor
republishes it.

Rows without a count are **excluded** when this is set. `/trending-projections` is the same
filter as a dedicated endpoint, pre-sorted; choose a threshold that fits your own use case.

starts_after.description:
**Only events starting at or after this instant.** Optional. ISO 8601, e.g.
`2026-09-09T00:00:00Z` or `2026-09-09T20:20:00-04:00`.

Compared as an instant, not as text, so an offset-bearing timestamp and a `Z` timestamp for the
same moment behave identically. The platform sends its own start times with a zone offset
(`2026-10-20T15:10:00.000-04:00`).

Pair with `starts_before` for a slate window. A season-long league such as `NFLSZN` has start
times months out, so a narrow window on those boards legitimately returns nothing.

starts_before.description:

`starts_after`.

`starts_before=2026-09-10T00:00:00Z` is one day's fixtures regardless of which zone the events
are played in.

silently return the whole board.

sort.description:
**How to order the results.** Optional; defaults to `rank` on the general boards and to
`trending_count` on `/trending-projections`. Leave it unset to get each endpoint's own default
ordering  -  naming a key here overrides it.

- `rank`  -  the platform's own board ordering, so an unsorted page looks like the app's board
- `line_score`  -  the number the line is set at (points, yards, goals  -  whatever the stat is)
- `start_time`  -  when the event tips off; pair with `desc` for the furthest-out lines
- `trending_count`  -  how many players have picked it; the popularity signal
- `player_name`  -  alphabetical by athlete
- `stat_type`  -  groups every "Rebounds" line together, then every "Points" line
- `updated_at`  -  most recently re-priced last, or first with `desc`; the freshness ordering

line with no `trending_count` never displaces one that has a real value.

sort_direction.description:
**Ascending or descending.** Optional; defaults to `asc` for every sort except
`/trending-projections`, which defaults to `desc` because the interesting end of a popularity
ranking is the top.

Accepts `asc` or `desc`. Rows with no value for the chosen sort key stay last in either
direction rather than flipping to the front on `desc`.

page.description:
**Which page of results to return.** Optional, 1-based, defaults to `1`  -  send `page=2` for
the second page.

Every paged response carries a `pagination` block  -  `{page, per_page, total, total_pages,
has_more}`  -  so you can drive a loop off `has_more` without guessing where the end is.

A page past the end is not an error: it returns an empty `projections` array with the true
`total` and `total_pages`, so a caller that overshoots gets a clean stop rather than a `404`.

per_page.description:
**How many results per page.** Optional, defaults to `50`, maximum `200`  -  e.g. `per_page=200`
to ingest a board in the fewest calls.

Use a small page while you are exploring a board and the maximum when you are ingesting one.
Use the response pagination block to determine how many pages remain; board sizes change with
the sports calendar.

Values above `200` are rejected rather than silently clamped, so a caller never believes they
received a full board when they received a capped one.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
**Filter by the line's own lifecycle state.** Optional. Case-insensitive exact match against
the projection's `status` field, e.g. `pre_game`.

This is deliberately **not** a closed list. The platform can add or expose states as its boards
change, so rejecting an unlisted value could block a state the source accepts. An unmatched value
returns an empty page instead.

**It is not the live signal, and this trips people up.** Rows on events already under way keep

different field from `game.status`, which is the FIXTURE's state and spells itself with a
hyphen (`pre-game`, `scheduled`) rather than an underscore.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
**How to order the results.** Optional; defaults to `rank` on the general boards and to
`trending_count` on `/trending-projections`. Leave it unset to get each endpoint's own default
ordering  -  naming a key here overrides it.

- `rank`  -  the platform's own board ordering, so an unsorted page looks like the app's board
- `line_score`  -  the number the line is set at (points, yards, goals  -  whatever the stat is)
- `start_time`  -  when the event tips off; pair with `desc` for the furthest-out lines
- `trending_count`  -  how many players have picked it; the popularity signal
- `player_name`  -  alphabetical by athlete
- `stat_type`  -  groups every "Rebounds" line together, then every "Points" line
- `updated_at`  -  most recently re-priced last, or first with `desc`; the freshness ordering

Sorting is stable, and rows missing the sort key are placed last in **both** directions, so a
line with no `trending_count` never displaces one that has a real value.

league.description:
**Which league's board to read.** Required on every board endpoint.

Accepts either the league **name** or its numeric **id**, and the name is case-insensitive  -  `NBA`,
`nba` and `7` all reach the same board.

**Board sizes move with the sports calendar**  -  an out-of-season league is a real league with zero
lines on it, not an error. Call `/leagues?with_projections_only=true` for the leagues that actually
have something on the board right now, and sort by `projections_count` to find the busiest.

**Very large boards may not support a board-wide read.** If one returns `503`, narrow the request
with `player_id` or `external_game_id`, or use `/projections-by-ids` or `/projection-details`.
The affected leagues move with the sports calendar, so discover them from `/leagues` rather than
hard-coding a list.

The catalogue includes period splits (`NFL1H`, `WNBA1Q`, `EPL2H`) and season-long markets
(`NFLSZN`, `NBASZN`). A name that does not match returns a `404` naming the
endpoint that lists them, never an empty success payload.

player_name.description:
**Filter to one athlete by name.** Optional. Case-insensitive substring, matched against both
the player's full name and their display name.

Examples: `Tatum`, `jayson tatum`, `Judge`. A partial surname is usually enough and is safer
than a full name  -  rosters spell accents and suffixes inconsistently.

For an exact, unambiguous lookup use `player_id` instead, or call `/player-projections`, which
returns the athlete's whole slate in one call.

player_id.description:
**Filter to one athlete by id.** Optional. Digits only, e.g. `59107`.

This is the platform's own player id, and it is the exact-match counterpart to `player_name`.
Read one off any projection's `player.id`, or off `/players`.

Player ids are global  -  the same athlete keeps the same id across every league they appear in
 -  but a board is still read one league at a time, so `league` stays required.

**Prefer this over `player_name` on very large boards.** An exact id allows the API to perform a
narrow lookup without requiring a board-wide read, so it can remain available when a name search
or an unfiltered request is not.

team.description:
**Filter to one team.** Optional. Case-insensitive substring, matched against the team
abbreviation, the nickname and the market.

So `BOS`, `Celtics` and `Boston` all reach the same rows. Abbreviations are the platform's own
(`BOS`, `NE`, `PIT`)  -  call `/teams?league=NBA` for the exact set on a board.

Because it is a substring match, a short string can over-match across sports (`LA` catches both
Los Angeles clubs). Prefer the nickname when you want exactly one club.

position.description:
**Filter to one roster position.** Optional. Exact match, case-insensitive.

Positions are **per-sport vocabularies**, spelled the way the platform spells them: `QB`, `RB`,
`WR`, `TE` in football; `F-G`, `G`, `C`, `F-C` in basketball; `SP`, `RP`, `C`, `1B` in baseball.
Combination slots use a hyphen (`F-G`), not a slash.

Read the live vocabulary for a board off `/players?league=NBA` rather than assuming a spelling  - 
an unmatched position returns an empty page, not an error.

stat_type.description:
**Filter to one stat market, exactly.** Optional. Case-insensitive exact match against both the
stat name and its display name.

Stat markets are **per-league vocabularies**, not one global list. Examples include `Points`,
`Assists`, `Rebounds`, `Pts+Asts`, `Rush Yards`, and `Strikeouts`; the available set changes by
league and as boards change.

Call `/stat-types?league=NBA` for the exact list before filtering. For a prefix or family match
(`Pts+` to catch all three combination markets) use `stat_type_contains` instead.

stat_type_contains.description:
**Filter to a family of stat markets.** Optional. Case-insensitive substring, matched against
the same two fields as `stat_type`.

This is the one to use for combination markets and period splits: `Pts+` catches `Pts+Asts`,
`Pts+Rebs` and `Pts+Rebs+Asts`; `Yards` catches `Rush Yards`, `Receiving Yards` and
`Pass Yards`; `Inning` catches every in-play baseball split.

Combine it with `stat_type` only if you mean both conditions  -  they narrow, they do not widen.

duration.description:
**Filter to one scoring period.** Optional. Exact match, case-insensitive, against the period
a line is scored over  -  `Full`, `1st Half`, `1Q`, `MAPS 1-2`, `1+2 Innings`, `MAP 4`.

Most boards use one period and this changes nothing on them; it matters when the same athlete and
stat are posted over different windows, such as multiple maps, halves, quarters, or inning ranges.

**Read the exact vocabulary for a board off `/board-summary`'s `counts_by_duration`** rather than
guessing a spelling  -  the values are per-sport and are spelled the way the platform spells them

value returns an empty page, not an error.

**Keep only lines on events already in play.** Optional; unset returns everything.

Set `true` to isolate in-play lines. **Do not filter on `status` for this**  -  the platform leaves
`status` at `pre_game` on live rows, and the reliable signals are the `is_live` and `in_game`
booleans this parameter reads.

Live inventory is concentrated in the dedicated in-play boards (`MLBLIVE`, `WNBA1H`, `NFL1H`) rather
than spread across the main ones, so pair this with the right `league`. `/live-projections` is the
same filter as a dedicated endpoint.

in_game.description:
**Split pre-game lines from in-play lines.** Optional, and it is a three-state filter.

- unset  -  return both
- `true`  -  only lines on events already under way
- `false`  -  only lines on events that have not started

Use `false` to strip live inventory out of a board you are ingesting for pre-game analysis. Use
`true` for the in-play slice  -  which is what `live_only` does, from the other side.

today_only.description:
**Keep only lines the platform flags as today's action.** Optional; unset returns everything.

Set `true` to trim a board down to the current slate. This reads the platform's own `today` flag
rather than comparing timestamps, so it follows the platform's notion of a sports day  -  which does
not end at midnight and is not your time zone's.

For an explicit window instead, use `starts_after` and `starts_before`.

min_line_score.description:
**Only lines set at or above this number.** Optional, inclusive.

The unit is whatever the stat is  -  points, yards, goals, strikeouts  -  so a bound is only
meaningful alongside a `stat_type`. `stat_type=Points&min_line_score=25` is a question; a bare
`min_line_score=25` mixes 25 rebounds with 25 receiving yards.

Lines with **no** `line_score` are excluded whenever either bound is set. A `0` line score is a
real, playable line and is never treated as missing.

max_line_score.description:
**Only lines set at or below this number.** Optional, inclusive.

Pair it with `min_line_score` for a window, or send it alone for a ceiling. Same unit caveat:
bound a single `stat_type` or the number means nothing.

Lines with no `line_score` are excluded whenever either bound is set.

min_trending_count.description:
**Only lines picked at least this many times.** Optional, inclusive.

`trending_count` is the platform's own pick-popularity signal  -  how many entries have taken
that line. It is PrizePicks-native crowd data, not a sportsbook handle split, and no competitor
republishes it.

Rows without a count are **excluded** when this is set. `/trending-projections` is the same
filter as a dedicated endpoint, pre-sorted; choose a threshold that fits your own use case.

starts_after.description:
**Only events starting at or after this instant.** Optional. ISO 8601, e.g.
`2026-09-09T00:00:00Z` or `2026-09-09T20:20:00-04:00`.

Compared as an instant, not as text, so an offset-bearing timestamp and a `Z` timestamp for the
same moment behave identically. The platform sends its own start times with a zone offset
(`2026-10-20T15:10:00.000-04:00`).

Pair with `starts_before` for a slate window. A season-long league such as `NFLSZN` has start
times months out, so a narrow window on those boards legitimately returns nothing.

starts_before.description:
**Only events starting at or before this instant.** Optional. ISO 8601, same format as
`starts_after`.

The two together bound a slate: `starts_after=2026-09-09T00:00:00Z` plus
`starts_before=2026-09-10T00:00:00Z` is one day's fixtures regardless of which zone the events
are played in.

An unparseable timestamp is rejected rather than ignored, so a malformed window can never
silently return the whole board.

sort.description:
**How to order the results.** Optional; defaults to `rank` on the general boards and to
`trending_count` on `/trending-projections`. Leave it unset to get each endpoint's own default
ordering  -  naming a key here overrides it.

- `rank`  -  the platform's own board ordering, so an unsorted page looks like the app's board
- `line_score`  -  the number the line is set at (points, yards, goals  -  whatever the stat is)
- `start_time`  -  when the event tips off; pair with `desc` for the furthest-out lines
- `trending_count`  -  how many players have picked it; the popularity signal
- `player_name`  -  alphabetical by athlete
- `stat_type`  -  groups every "Rebounds" line together, then every "Points" line
- `updated_at`  -  most recently re-priced last, or first with `desc`; the freshness ordering

Sorting is stable, and rows missing the sort key are placed last in **both** directions, so a
line with no `trending_count` never displaces one that has a real value.

sort_direction.description:
**Ascending or descending.** Optional; defaults to `asc` for every sort except
`/trending-projections`, which defaults to `desc` because the interesting end of a popularity
ranking is the top.

Accepts `asc` or `desc`. Rows with no value for the chosen sort key stay last in either
direction rather than flipping to the front on `desc`.

page.description:
**Which page of results to return.** Optional, 1-based, defaults to `1`  -  send `page=2` for
the second page.

Every paged response carries a `pagination` block  -  `{page, per_page, total, total_pages,
has_more}`  -  so you can drive a loop off `has_more` without guessing where the end is.

A page past the end is not an error: it returns an empty `projections` array with the true
`total` and `total_pages`, so a caller that overshoots gets a clean stop rather than a `404`.

per_page.description:
**How many results per page.** Optional, defaults to `50`, maximum `200`  -  e.g. `per_page=200`
to ingest a board in the fewest calls.

Use a small page while you are exploring a board and the maximum when you are ingesting one.
Use the response pagination block to determine how many pages remain; board sizes change with
the sports calendar.

Values above `200` are rejected rather than silently clamped, so a caller never believes they
received a full board when they received a capped one.

parameters.name: league
parameters.description:
**Which league's board to read.** Required on every board endpoint.

Accepts either the league **name** or its numeric **id**, and the name is case-insensitive  -  `NBA`,
`nba` and `7` all reach the same board.

**Board sizes move with the sports calendar**  -  an out-of-season league is a real league with zero
lines on it, not an error. Call `/leagues?with_projections_only=true` for the leagues that actually
have something on the board right now, and sort by `projections_count` to find the busiest.

**Very large boards may not support a board-wide read.** If one returns `503`, narrow the request
with `player_id` or `external_game_id`, or use `/projections-by-ids` or `/projection-details`.
The affected leagues move with the sports calendar, so discover them from `/leagues` rather than
hard-coding a list.

The catalogue includes period splits (`NFL1H`, `WNBA1Q`, `EPL2H`) and season-long markets
(`NFLSZN`, `NBASZN`). A name that does not match returns a `404` naming the
endpoint that lists them, never an empty success payload.

league.description:
**Which league's board to read.** Required on every board endpoint.

Accepts either the league **name** or its numeric **id**, and the name is case-insensitive  -  `NBA`,
`nba` and `7` all reach the same board.

**Board sizes move with the sports calendar**  -  an out-of-season league is a real league with zero
lines on it, not an error. Call `/leagues?with_projections_only=true` for the leagues that actually
have something on the board right now, and sort by `projections_count` to find the busiest.

**Very large boards may not support a board-wide read.** If one returns `503`, narrow the request
with `player_id` or `external_game_id`, or use `/projections-by-ids` or `/projection-details`.
The affected leagues move with the sports calendar, so discover them from `/leagues` rather than
hard-coding a list.

The catalogue includes period splits (`NFL1H`, `WNBA1Q`, `EPL2H`) and season-long markets
(`NFLSZN`, `NBASZN`). A name that does not match returns a `404` naming the
endpoint that lists them, never an empty success payload.

player_name.description:
**Filter to one athlete by name.** Optional. Case-insensitive substring, matched against both
the player's full name and their display name.

Examples: `Tatum`, `jayson tatum`, `Judge`. A partial surname is usually enough and is safer
than a full name  -  rosters spell accents and suffixes inconsistently.

For an exact, unambiguous lookup use `player_id` instead, or call `/player-projections`, which
returns the athlete's whole slate in one call.

player_id.description:
**Filter to one athlete by id.** Optional. Digits only, e.g. `59107`.

This is the platform's own player id, and it is the exact-match counterpart to `player_name`.
Read one off any projection's `player.id`, or off `/players`.

Player ids are global  -  the same athlete keeps the same id across every league they appear in
 -  but a board is still read one league at a time, so `league` stays required.

**Prefer this over `player_name` on very large boards.** An exact id allows the API to perform a
narrow lookup without requiring a board-wide read, so it can remain available when a name search
or an unfiltered request is not.

team.description:
**Filter to one team.** Optional. Case-insensitive substring, matched against the team
abbreviation, the nickname and the market.

So `BOS`, `Celtics` and `Boston` all reach the same rows. Abbreviations are the platform's own
(`BOS`, `NE`, `PIT`)  -  call `/teams?league=NBA` for the exact set on a board.

Because it is a substring match, a short string can over-match across sports (`LA` catches both
Los Angeles clubs). Prefer the nickname when you want exactly one club.

position.description:
**Filter to one roster position.** Optional. Exact match, case-insensitive.

Positions are **per-sport vocabularies**, spelled the way the platform spells them: `QB`, `RB`,
`WR`, `TE` in football; `F-G`, `G`, `C`, `F-C` in basketball; `SP`, `RP`, `C`, `1B` in baseball.
Combination slots use a hyphen (`F-G`), not a slash.

Read the live vocabulary for a board off `/players?league=NBA` rather than assuming a spelling  - 
an unmatched position returns an empty page, not an error.

stat_type.description:
**Filter to one stat market, exactly.** Optional. Case-insensitive exact match against both the
stat name and its display name.

Stat markets are **per-league vocabularies**, not one global list. Examples include `Points`,
`Assists`, `Rebounds`, `Pts+Asts`, `Rush Yards`, and `Strikeouts`; the available set changes by
league and as boards change.

Call `/stat-types?league=NBA` for the exact list before filtering. For a prefix or family match
(`Pts+` to catch all three combination markets) use `stat_type_contains` instead.

stat_type_contains.description:
**Filter to a family of stat markets.** Optional. Case-insensitive substring, matched against
the same two fields as `stat_type`.

This is the one to use for combination markets and period splits: `Pts+` catches `Pts+Asts`,
`Pts+Rebs` and `Pts+Rebs+Asts`; `Yards` catches `Rush Yards`, `Receiving Yards` and
`Pass Yards`; `Inning` catches every in-play baseball split.

Combine it with `stat_type` only if you mean both conditions  -  they narrow, they do not widen.

**Filter to one scoring period.** Optional. Exact match, case-insensitive, against the period
a line is scored over  -  `Full`, `1st Half`, `1Q`, `MAPS 1-2`, `1+2 Innings`, `MAP 4`.

Most boards use one period and this changes nothing on them; it matters when the same athlete and
stat are posted over different windows, such as multiple maps, halves, quarters, or inning ranges.

**Read the exact vocabulary for a board off `/board-summary`'s `counts_by_duration`** rather than
guessing a spelling  -  the values are per-sport and are spelled the way the platform spells them
(`1st Half` on the football half board, `1H` on the football-league half board). An unmatched
value returns an empty page, not an error.

**Filter by the Demon/Goblin dimension.** Optional. This is the field a plain line feed leaves
out, and it is what makes a line comparable to a price.

- `demon`  -  a harder line at a bigger payout
- `goblin`  -  an easier line at a smaller payout
- `standard`  -  the normal line

A PrizePicks entry carries a line rather than a price, so `odds_type` plus `line_score` is how
you reason about value here  -  an odds aggregator that only republishes the number cannot tell
you which of the three you are looking at.

**Filter by what kind of projection it is.** Optional. Two values, spelled as the platform
spells them (spaced and title-cased, not snake_case):

- `Fantasy Score`  -  a composite fantasy total rather than a raw stat

Filter to `Fantasy Score` when you want the composite markets isolated; most callers want the
default, which is both.

**Filter by what the line is attached to.** Optional. Six values:

- `matchup`  -  one athlete measured against another
- `team_with_duration`  -  scoped to a period or inning (see `duration` on each row)

with start times months apart.

league.description:
**Which league's board to read.** Required on every board endpoint.

Accepts either the league **name** or its numeric **id**, and the name is case-insensitive  -  `NBA`,
`nba` and `7` all reach the same board.

**Board sizes move with the sports calendar**  -  an out-of-season league is a real league with zero
lines on it, not an error. Call `/leagues?with_projections_only=true` for the leagues that actually
have something on the board right now, and sort by `projections_count` to find the busiest.

**Very large boards may not support a board-wide read.** If one returns `503`, narrow the request
with `player_id` or `external_game_id`, or use `/projections-by-ids` or `/projection-details`.
The affected leagues move with the sports calendar, so discover them from `/leagues` rather than
hard-coding a list.

The catalogue includes period splits (`NFL1H`, `WNBA1Q`, `EPL2H`) and season-long markets
(`NFLSZN`, `NBASZN`). A name that does not match returns a `404` naming the
endpoint that lists them, never an empty success payload.

player_name.description:
**Filter to one athlete by name.** Optional. Case-insensitive substring, matched against both
the player's full name and their display name.

Examples: `Tatum`, `jayson tatum`, `Judge`. A partial surname is usually enough and is safer
than a full name  -  rosters spell accents and suffixes inconsistently.

For an exact, unambiguous lookup use `player_id` instead, or call `/player-projections`, which
returns the athlete's whole slate in one call.

player_id.description:
**Filter to one athlete by id.** Optional. Digits only, e.g. `59107`.

This is the platform's own player id, and it is the exact-match counterpart to `player_name`.
Read one off any projection's `player.id`, or off `/players`.

Player ids are global  -  the same athlete keeps the same id across every league they appear in
 -  but a board is still read one league at a time, so `league` stays required.

**Prefer this over `player_name` on very large boards.** An exact id allows the API to perform a
narrow lookup without requiring a board-wide read, so it can remain available when a name search
or an unfiltered request is not.

team.description:
**Filter to one team.** Optional. Case-insensitive substring, matched against the team
abbreviation, the nickname and the market.

So `BOS`, `Celtics` and `Boston` all reach the same rows. Abbreviations are the platform's own
(`BOS`, `NE`, `PIT`)  -  call `/teams?league=NBA` for the exact set on a board.

Because it is a substring match, a short string can over-match across sports (`LA` catches both
Los Angeles clubs). Prefer the nickname when you want exactly one club.

position.description:
**Filter to one roster position.** Optional. Exact match, case-insensitive.

Positions are **per-sport vocabularies**, spelled the way the platform spells them: `QB`, `RB`,
`WR`, `TE` in football; `F-G`, `G`, `C`, `F-C` in basketball; `SP`, `RP`, `C`, `1B` in baseball.
Combination slots use a hyphen (`F-G`), not a slash.

Read the live vocabulary for a board off `/players?league=NBA` rather than assuming a spelling  - 
an unmatched position returns an empty page, not an error.

stat_type.description:
**Filter to one stat market, exactly.** Optional. Case-insensitive exact match against both the
stat name and its display name.

Stat markets are **per-league vocabularies**, not one global list. Examples include `Points`,
`Assists`, `Rebounds`, `Pts+Asts`, `Rush Yards`, and `Strikeouts`; the available set changes by
league and as boards change.

Call `/stat-types?league=NBA` for the exact list before filtering. For a prefix or family match
(`Pts+` to catch all three combination markets) use `stat_type_contains` instead.

stat_type_contains.description:
**Filter to a family of stat markets.** Optional. Case-insensitive substring, matched against
the same two fields as `stat_type`.

This is the one to use for combination markets and period splits: `Pts+` catches `Pts+Asts`,
`Pts+Rebs` and `Pts+Rebs+Asts`; `Yards` catches `Rush Yards`, `Receiving Yards` and
`Pass Yards`; `Inning` catches every in-play baseball split.

Combine it with `stat_type` only if you mean both conditions  -  they narrow, they do not widen.

duration.description:
**Filter to one scoring period.** Optional. Exact match, case-insensitive, against the period
a line is scored over  -  `Full`, `1st Half`, `1Q`, `MAPS 1-2`, `1+2 Innings`, `MAP 4`.

Most boards use one period and this changes nothing on them; it matters when the same athlete and
stat are posted over different windows, such as multiple maps, halves, quarters, or inning ranges.

**Read the exact vocabulary for a board off `/board-summary`'s `counts_by_duration`** rather than
guessing a spelling  -  the values are per-sport and are spelled the way the platform spells them
(`1st Half` on the football half board, `1H` on the football-league half board). An unmatched
value returns an empty page, not an error.

odds_type.description:
**Filter by the Demon/Goblin dimension.** Optional. This is the field a plain line feed leaves
out, and it is what makes a line comparable to a price.

- `demon`  -  a harder line at a bigger payout
- `goblin`  -  an easier line at a smaller payout
- `standard`  -  the normal line

A PrizePicks entry carries a line rather than a price, so `odds_type` plus `line_score` is how
you reason about value here  -  an odds aggregator that only republishes the number cannot tell
you which of the three you are looking at.

projection_type.description:
**Filter by what kind of projection it is.** Optional. Two values, spelled as the platform
spells them (spaced and title-cased, not snake_case):

- `Single Stat`  -  one measurable stat for one athlete
- `Fantasy Score`  -  a composite fantasy total rather than a raw stat

Filter to `Fantasy Score` when you want the composite markets isolated; most callers want the
default, which is both.

event_type.description:
**Filter by what the line is attached to.** Optional. Six values:

- `team`  -  an athlete in a specific fixture, the ordinary case
- `seasonal`  -  a season-long total, the `…SZN` league boards
- `matchup`  -  one athlete measured against another
- `team_with_duration`  -  scoped to a period or inning (see `duration` on each row)
- `combo`  -  a combined line across more than one athlete
- `event`  -  attached to an event rather than a fixture (a race, a card)

Use `seasonal` to separate futures from same-day action  -  they otherwise sit on the same board
with start times months apart.

allowed_wager_types.description:
**Filter by which way a line can be played.** Optional.

- `under_or_over`  -  playable in both directions
- `over`  -  over-only

Rows with **no** value for this field are excluded whenever this filter is set  -  a missing value
is not a third bucket, and folding it into one of the two would publish a wager direction the
platform never stated.

status.description:
**Filter by the line's own lifecycle state.** Optional. Case-insensitive exact match against
the projection's `status` field, e.g. `pre_game`.

This is deliberately **not** a closed list. The platform can add or expose states as its boards
change, so rejecting an unlisted value could block a state the source accepts. An unmatched value
returns an empty page instead.

**It is not the live signal, and this trips people up.** Rows on events already under way keep
`status: "pre_game"` on this host. Use `live_only` or `in_game` for in-play lines. It is also a
different field from `game.status`, which is the FIXTURE's state and spells itself with a
hyphen (`pre-game`, `scheduled`) rather than an underscore.

game_id.description:
**Filter to one fixture by its internal id.** Optional. Digits only, e.g. `181166`.

This is the platform's own numeric game id  -  the `game.id` on every projection and the `id` on
every row of `/games`. It is the shorter of the two game identifiers the platform carries.

The other one is `external_game_id`, the feed key (`NBA_game_MXorbpoalrXOT11KmdzI3Vn6`). They
address the same fixture; use whichever you already have.

external_game_id.description:
**Filter to one fixture by its feed key.** Optional. The long form, e.g.
`NBA_game_MXorbpoalrXOT11KmdzI3Vn6`.

This is the identifier that travels with the platform's data feed and appears as
`external_game_id` on `/games` and on every projection's `game` object. It is stable across the
life of a fixture and is the id to key on if you are joining against your own schedule data.

The numeric `game_id` addresses the same fixture more compactly  -  but **prefer this form on very
large boards.** The feed key allows a narrow lookup without requiring a board-wide read, so it
can remain available when the numeric-id form or an unfiltered request is not.

live_only.description:
**Keep only lines on events already in play.** Optional; unset returns everything.

Set `true` to isolate in-play lines. **Do not filter on `status` for this**  -  the platform leaves
`status` at `pre_game` on live rows, and the reliable signals are the `is_live` and `in_game`
booleans this parameter reads.

Live inventory is concentrated in the dedicated in-play boards (`MLBLIVE`, `WNBA1H`, `NFL1H`) rather
than spread across the main ones, so pair this with the right `league`. `/live-projections` is the
same filter as a dedicated endpoint.

in_game.description:
**Split pre-game lines from in-play lines.** Optional, and it is a three-state filter.

- unset  -  return both
- `true`  -  only lines on events already under way
- `false`  -  only lines on events that have not started

Use `false` to strip live inventory out of a board you are ingesting for pre-game analysis. Use
`true` for the in-play slice  -  which is what `live_only` does, from the other side.

today_only.description:
**Keep only lines the platform flags as today's action.** Optional; unset returns everything.

Set `true` to trim a board down to the current slate. This reads the platform's own `today` flag
rather than comparing timestamps, so it follows the platform's notion of a sports day  -  which does
not end at midnight and is not your time zone's.

For an explicit window instead, use `starts_after` and `starts_before`.

min_line_score.description:
**Only lines set at or above this number.** Optional, inclusive.

The unit is whatever the stat is  -  points, yards, goals, strikeouts  -  so a bound is only
meaningful alongside a `stat_type`. `stat_type=Points&min_line_score=25` is a question; a bare
`min_line_score=25` mixes 25 rebounds with 25 receiving yards.

Lines with **no** `line_score` are excluded whenever either bound is set. A `0` line score is a
real, playable line and is never treated as missing.

max_line_score.description:
**Only lines set at or below this number.** Optional, inclusive.

Pair it with `min_line_score` for a window, or send it alone for a ceiling. Same unit caveat:
bound a single `stat_type` or the number means nothing.

Lines with no `line_score` are excluded whenever either bound is set.

min_trending_count.description:
**Only lines picked at least this many times.** Optional, inclusive.

`trending_count` is the platform's own pick-popularity signal  -  how many entries have taken
that line. It is PrizePicks-native crowd data, not a sportsbook handle split, and no competitor
republishes it.

Rows without a count are **excluded** when this is set. `/trending-projections` is the same
filter as a dedicated endpoint, pre-sorted; choose a threshold that fits your own use case.

starts_after.description:
**Only events starting at or after this instant.** Optional. ISO 8601, e.g.
`2026-09-09T00:00:00Z` or `2026-09-09T20:20:00-04:00`.

Compared as an instant, not as text, so an offset-bearing timestamp and a `Z` timestamp for the
same moment behave identically. The platform sends its own start times with a zone offset
(`2026-10-20T15:10:00.000-04:00`).

Pair with `starts_before` for a slate window. A season-long league such as `NFLSZN` has start
times months out, so a narrow window on those boards legitimately returns nothing.

starts_before.description:
**Only events starting at or before this instant.** Optional. ISO 8601, same format as
`starts_after`.

The two together bound a slate: `starts_after=2026-09-09T00:00:00Z` plus
`starts_before=2026-09-10T00:00:00Z` is one day's fixtures regardless of which zone the events
are played in.

An unparseable timestamp is rejected rather than ignored, so a malformed window can never
silently return the whole board.

sort.description:
**How to order the results.** Optional; defaults to `rank` on the general boards and to
`trending_count` on `/trending-projections`. Leave it unset to get each endpoint's own default
ordering  -  naming a key here overrides it.

- `rank`  -  the platform's own board ordering, so an unsorted page looks like the app's board
- `line_score`  -  the number the line is set at (points, yards, goals  -  whatever the stat is)
- `start_time`  -  when the event tips off; pair with `desc` for the furthest-out lines
- `trending_count`  -  how many players have picked it; the popularity signal
- `player_name`  -  alphabetical by athlete
- `stat_type`  -  groups every "Rebounds" line together, then every "Points" line
- `updated_at`  -  most recently re-priced last, or first with `desc`; the freshness ordering

Sorting is stable, and rows missing the sort key are placed last in **both** directions, so a
line with no `trending_count` never displaces one that has a real value.

sort_direction.description:
**Ascending or descending.** Optional; defaults to `asc` for every sort except
`/trending-projections`, which defaults to `desc` because the interesting end of a popularity
ranking is the top.

Accepts `asc` or `desc`. Rows with no value for the chosen sort key stay last in either
direction rather than flipping to the front on `desc`.

page.description:
**Which page of results to return.** Optional, 1-based, defaults to `1`  -  send `page=2` for
the second page.

Every paged response carries a `pagination` block  -  `{page, per_page, total, total_pages,
has_more}`  -  so you can drive a loop off `has_more` without guessing where the end is.

A page past the end is not an error: it returns an empty `projections` array with the true
`total` and `total_pages`, so a caller that overshoots gets a clean stop rather than a `404`.

per_page.description:
**How many results per page.** Optional, defaults to `50`, maximum `200`  -  e.g. `per_page=200`
to ingest a board in the fewest calls.

Use a small page while you are exploring a board and the maximum when you are ingesting one.
Use the response pagination block to determine how many pages remain; board sizes change with
the sports calendar.

Values above `200` are rejected rather than silently clamped, so a caller never believes they
received a full board when they received a capped one.

parameters.name: league
parameters.description:
**Which league's board to read.** Required on every board endpoint.

Accepts either the league **name** or its numeric **id**, and the name is case-insensitive  -  `NBA`,
`nba` and `7` all reach the same board.

**Board sizes move with the sports calendar**  -  an out-of-season league is a real league with zero
lines on it, not an error. Call `/leagues?with_projections_only=true` for the leagues that actually
have something on the board right now, and sort by `projections_count` to find the busiest.

**Very large boards may not support a board-wide read.** If one returns `503`, narrow the request
with `player_id` or `external_game_id`, or use `/projections-by-ids` or `/projection-details`.
The affected leagues move with the sports calendar, so discover them from `/leagues` rather than
hard-coding a list.

The catalogue includes period splits (`NFL1H`, `WNBA1Q`, `EPL2H`) and season-long markets
(`NFLSZN`, `NBASZN`). A name that does not match returns a `404` naming the
endpoint that lists them, never an empty success payload.

league.description:
**Which league's board to read.** Required on every board endpoint.

Accepts either the league **name** or its numeric **id**, and the name is case-insensitive  -  `NBA`,
`nba` and `7` all reach the same board.

**Board sizes move with the sports calendar**  -  an out-of-season league is a real league with zero
lines on it, not an error. Call `/leagues?with_projections_only=true` for the leagues that actually
have something on the board right now, and sort by `projections_count` to find the busiest.

**Very large boards may not support a board-wide read.** If one returns `503`, narrow the request
with `player_id` or `external_game_id`, or use `/projections-by-ids` or `/projection-details`.
The affected leagues move with the sports calendar, so discover them from `/leagues` rather than
hard-coding a list.

The catalogue includes period splits (`NFL1H`, `WNBA1Q`, `EPL2H`) and season-long markets
(`NFLSZN`, `NBASZN`). A name that does not match returns a `404` naming the
endpoint that lists them, never an empty success payload.

**Filter to one athlete by name.** Optional. Case-insensitive substring, matched against both
the player's full name and their display name.

Examples: `Tatum`, `jayson tatum`, `Judge`. A partial surname is usually enough and is safer
than a full name  -  rosters spell accents and suffixes inconsistently.

For an exact, unambiguous lookup use `player_id` instead, or call `/player-projections`, which
returns the athlete's whole slate in one call.

player_id.description:
**Filter to one athlete by id.** Optional. Digits only, e.g. `59107`.

This is the platform's own player id, and it is the exact-match counterpart to `player_name`.
Read one off any projection's `player.id`, or off `/players`.

Player ids are global  -  the same athlete keeps the same id across every league they appear in

**Prefer this over `player_name` on very large boards.** An exact id allows the API to perform a
narrow lookup without requiring a board-wide read, so it can remain available when a name search
or an unfiltered request is not.

**Filter to one team.** Optional. Case-insensitive substring, matched against the team
abbreviation, the nickname and the market.

So `BOS`, `Celtics` and `Boston` all reach the same rows. Abbreviations are the platform's own
(`BOS`, `NE`, `PIT`)  -  call `/teams?league=NBA` for the exact set on a board.

Because it is a substring match, a short string can over-match across sports (`LA` catches both
Los Angeles clubs). Prefer the nickname when you want exactly one club.

position.description:
**Filter to one roster position.** Optional. Exact match, case-insensitive.

Positions are **per-sport vocabularies**, spelled the way the platform spells them: `QB`, `RB`,
`WR`, `TE` in football; `F-G`, `G`, `C`, `F-C` in basketball; `SP`, `RP`, `C`, `1B` in baseball.
Combination slots use a hyphen (`F-G`), not a slash.

Read the live vocabulary for a board off `/players?league=NBA` rather than assuming a spelling  - 
an unmatched position returns an empty page, not an error.

stat_type.description:
**Filter to one stat market, exactly.** Optional. Case-insensitive exact match against both the
stat name and its display name.

league and as boards change.

Call `/stat-types?league=NBA` for the exact list before filtering. For a prefix or family match

duration.description:

- `goblin`  -  an easier line at a smaller payout

`trending_count` is the platform's own pick-popularity signal  -  how many entries have taken
that line. It is PrizePicks-native crowd data, not a sportsbook handle split, and no competitor
republishes it.

Rows without a count are **excluded** when this is set. `/trending-projections` is the same
filter as a dedicated endpoint, pre-sorted; choose a threshold that fits your own use case.

starts_after.description:
**Only events starting at or after this instant.** Optional. ISO 8601, e.g.
`2026-09-09T00:00:00Z` or `2026-09-09T20:20:00-04:00`.

Compared as an instant, not as text, so an offset-bearing timestamp and a `Z` timestamp for the
same moment behave identically. The platform sends its own start times with a zone offset
(`2026-10-20T15:10:00.000-04:00`).

Pair with `starts_before` for a slate window. A season-long league such as `NFLSZN` has start
times months out, so a narrow window on those boards legitimately returns nothing.

starts_before.description:
**Only events starting at or before this instant.** Optional. ISO 8601, same format as
`starts_after`.

The two together bound a slate: `starts_after=2026-09-09T00:00:00Z` plus
`starts_before=2026-09-10T00:00:00Z` is one day's fixtures regardless of which zone the events
are played in.

An unparseable timestamp is rejected rather than ignored, so a malformed window can never
silently return the whole board.

sort.description:
**How to order the results.** Optional; defaults to `rank` on the general boards and to
`trending_count` on `/trending-projections`. Leave it unset to get each endpoint's own default
ordering  -  naming a key here overrides it.

- `rank`  -  the platform's own board ordering, so an unsorted page looks like the app's board
- `line_score`  -  the number the line is set at (points, yards, goals  -  whatever the stat is)
- `start_time`  -  when the event tips off; pair with `desc` for the furthest-out lines
- `trending_count`  -  how many players have picked it; the popularity signal
- `player_name`  -  alphabetical by athlete
- `stat_type`  -  groups every "Rebounds" line together, then every "Points" line
- `updated_at`  -  most recently re-priced last, or first with `desc`; the freshness ordering

Sorting is stable, and rows missing the sort key are placed last in **both** directions, so a
line with no `trending_count` never displaces one that has a real value.

sort_direction.description:
**Ascending or descending.** Optional; defaults to `asc` for every sort except
`/trending-projections`, which defaults to `desc` because the interesting end of a popularity
ranking is the top.

Accepts `asc` or `desc`. Rows with no value for the chosen sort key stay last in either
direction rather than flipping to the front on `desc`.

page.description:
**Which page of results to return.** Optional, 1-based, defaults to `1`  -  send `page=2` for
the second page.

Every paged response carries a `pagination` block  -  `{page, per_page, total, total_pages,
has_more}`  -  so you can drive a loop off `has_more` without guessing where the end is.

A page past the end is not an error: it returns an empty `projections` array with the true
`total` and `total_pages`, so a caller that overshoots gets a clean stop rather than a `404`.

per_page.description:
**How many results per page.** Optional, defaults to `50`, maximum `200`  -  e.g. `per_page=200`
to ingest a board in the fewest calls.

Use a small page while you are exploring a board and the maximum when you are ingesting one.
Use the response pagination block to determine how many pages remain; board sizes change with
the sports calendar.

Values above `200` are rejected rather than silently clamped, so a caller never believes they
received a full board when they received a capped one.

parameters.name: league
parameters.description:
**Which league's board to read.** Required on every board endpoint.

Accepts either the league **name** or its numeric **id**, and the name is case-insensitive  -  `NBA`,
`nba` and `7` all reach the same board.

**Board sizes move with the sports calendar**  -  an out-of-season league is a real league with zero
lines on it, not an error. Call `/leagues?with_projections_only=true` for the leagues that actually
have something on the board right now, and sort by `projections_count` to find the busiest.

**Very large boards may not support a board-wide read.** If one returns `503`, narrow the request
with `player_id` or `external_game_id`, or use `/projections-by-ids` or `/projection-details`.
The affected leagues move with the sports calendar, so discover them from `/leagues` rather than
hard-coding a list.

The catalogue includes period splits (`NFL1H`, `WNBA1Q`, `EPL2H`) and season-long markets
(`NFLSZN`, `NBASZN`). A name that does not match returns a `404` naming the
endpoint that lists them, never an empty success payload.

Accepts either the league **name** or its numeric **id**, and the name is case-insensitive  -  `NBA`,
`nba` and `7` all reach the same board.

**Board sizes move with the sports calendar**  -  an out-of-season league is a real league with zero
lines on it, not an error. Call `/leagues?with_projections_only=true` for the leagues that actually
have something on the board right now, and sort by `projections_count` to find the busiest.

**Very large boards may not support a board-wide read.** If one returns `503`, narrow the request
with `player_id` or `external_game_id`, or use `/projections-by-ids` or `/projection-details`.
The affected leagues move with the sports calendar, so discover them from `/leagues` rather than
hard-coding a list.

The catalogue includes period splits (`NFL1H`, `WNBA1Q`, `EPL2H`) and season-long markets
(`NFLSZN`, `NBASZN`). A name that does not match returns a `404` naming the
endpoint that lists them, never an empty success payload.

parameters.name: player_id
parameters.description:
**Filter to one athlete by id.** Optional. Digits only, e.g. `59107`.

This is the platform's own player id, and it is the exact-match counterpart to `player_name`.
Read one off any projection's `player.id`, or off `/players`.

Player ids are global  -  the same athlete keeps the same id across every league they appear in
 -  but a board is still read one league at a time, so `league` stays required.

**Prefer this over `player_name` on very large boards.** An exact id allows the API to perform a
narrow lookup without requiring a board-wide read, so it can remain available when a name search
or an unfiltered request is not.

returns the athlete's whole slate in one call.

parameters.name: live_only

**Keep only lines on events already in play.** Optional; unset returns everything.

than spread across the main ones, so pair this with the right `league`. `/live-projections` is the
same filter as a dedicated endpoint.

parameters.name: team
parameters.description:
**Filter to the fixtures one club is playing in.** Optional. Case-insensitive substring,
matched against **both** sides of the fixture  -  each club's abbreviation, nickname and
market  -  so `SEA`, `Seahawks` and `Seattle` all reach the same games, home or away.

Note this is the FIXTURE's club, not the athlete's: the same parameter name on
`/projections` narrows by who the line is on. Here it answers "when is this club next out".

Participant data comes from the fixture's own home/away join where the platform ships it,
and falls back to the abbreviations in the fixture `metadata` where it does not  -  a handful
of boards (NBA preseason, most individual-athlete sports) carry neither, and their fixtures
cannot be matched by club at all. Because it is a substring match, a short string can
over-match across a league (`LA` catches both Los Angeles clubs); prefer the nickname.

parameters.name: starts_after
parameters.description:
**Only events starting at or after this instant.** Optional. ISO 8601, e.g.
`2026-09-09T00:00:00Z` or `2026-09-09T20:20:00-04:00`.

Compared as an instant, not as text, so an offset-bearing timestamp and a `Z` timestamp for the
same moment behave identically. The platform sends its own start times with a zone offset
(`2026-10-20T15:10:00.000-04:00`).

Pair with `starts_before` for a slate window. A season-long league such as `NFLSZN` has start
times months out, so a narrow window on those boards legitimately returns nothing.
